The trial in `02-community-shift.qmd` asked whether the community changed from
pre to post and whether that change differed by arm, averaged over everyone.
Averages can hide subgroups: the probiotic might have helped only the people
whose vaginal community was *already* a certain way at the start, and diluted
everyone else.

This report asks a third question:

3. **Does the effect of the probiotic depend on the community the participant
   started with?**

"Started a certain way" we define simply: at the pre visit, did Lactobacillus
make up at least 10% of the microbiome (we call these **Lactobacillus-present**)
or less (we call these **Lactobacillus-low**)? Lactobacillus is the genus a
healthy vaginal community is usually built around, so it is the natural way to
split the starting states.

"Worked" we measure three ways, all per participant (post minus pre):

- **Nugent score** fell (a clinical score of vaginal dysbiosis; lower is healthier)
- **pH** fell (a healthy vaginal pH is low, roughly under 4.5)
- **Amine test** flipped from Positive to Negative (a whiff-test sign of dysbiosis)

One workshop rule shapes the whole design: **define a group from one table, test
it on another.** We define the starting groups from the *microbiome* table, then
test the response in the *clinical metadata* and the *gene* table. We never test
the microbiome's own Lactobacillus change against a group defined by
Lactobacillus — that would be circular (see the caution in section 5).

## 2. Data

```{r setup}
library(tidyverse)
library(here)
library(DESeq2)

source(here("R/count_tables.R"))

d <- read_counts("group_a")

# Share of the community made up by Lactobacillus, per sample.
lacto_rows <- grep("Lactobacillus", d$taxonomy$Genus)
lacto_share <- colSums(prop.table(d$species, 2)[lacto_rows, , drop = FALSE])

# One row per participant: baseline state + the pre-to-post changes.
meta <- d$metadata |> mutate(lacto_share = lacto_share[sample_id])
participants <- meta |>
  filter(time_point == "pre") |>
  select(participant_id, arm, pre_share = lacto_share,
         pre_ph = ph, pre_nugent = nugent, pre_amine = amine_test) |>
  left_join(meta |>
              filter(time_point == "post") |>
              select(participant_id, post_ph = ph, post_nugent = nugent,
                     post_amine = amine_test),
            by = "participant_id") |>
  mutate(
    start   = if_else(pre_share >= 0.10, "Lacto-present", "Lacto-low"),
    chg_ph     = post_ph - pre_ph,
    chg_nugent = post_nugent - pre_nugent,
    amine_ok   = pre_amine == "Positive" & post_amine == "Negative"
  )
participants
```

```{r who}
participants |> dplyr::count(arm, start) |>   # dplyr:: because DESeq2 masks count()
  mutate(share = round(n / sum(n) * 100)) |>
  mutate(share = round(n / sum(n) * 100)) |>
  arrange(arm, start)
```

Most participants (131 of 176) started Lactobacillus-low; the community in this
cohort is broadly dysbiotic at baseline. Every arm × start group has at least 15
participants, so all four cells are worth looking at, though the Lacto-present
cells are small.

## 3. Where each participant started

```{r baseline-plot, fig.width=7, fig.height=3}
ggplot(participants, aes(pre_share)) +
  geom_histogram(bins = 40, fill = "#2b7bb9", colour = "white") +
  geom_vline(xintercept = 0.10, linetype = "dashed", colour = "#c46a3f") +
  scale_x_continuous(labels = scales::percent) +
  labs(title = "Lactobacillus share of the community at the pre visit",
       subtitle = "The dashed line is the 10% cut that defines the two starting groups",
       x = "Lactobacillus share at pre", y = "Participants") +
  theme_minimal()
```

The 10% cut is a choice, not a law of nature. The distribution is continuous
with a long tail; about half the cohort sits under 3%. Section 6 records the
alternatives we did not choose.

## 4. Did the clinical outcomes move differently?

For each outcome we fit a linear model of the form
`change ~ arm * start`. The `arm:start` interaction term is the answer to our
question: it asks whether the probiotic's effect (probiotic minus placebo) was
itself different in the two starting groups. A small p-value would say yes,
the effect depended on where the community started.

```{r clinical}
tests <- tribble(
  ~outcome, ~formula,
  "Nugent score change", "chg_nugent ~ arm * start",
  "pH change",           "chg_ph ~ arm * start"
)
tests |>
  mutate(p_interaction = map_dbl(formula, ~ summary(lm(.x, participants))$coefficients["armprobiotic:startLacto-present", "Pr(>|t|)"])) |>
  mutate(p_interaction = signif(p_interaction, 2))
```

```{r clinical-means}
participants |>
  filter(!is.na(chg_nugent), !is.na(chg_ph)) |>
  group_by(arm, start) |>
  summarise(n = n(),
            `mean Nugent change` = round(mean(chg_nugent), 1),
            `mean pH change`     = round(mean(chg_ph), 2),
            .groups = "drop")
```

```{r amine}
participants |>
  filter(pre_amine == "Positive") |>
  group_by(arm, start) |>
  summarise(n = n(),
            `% amine Positive -> Negative` = round(mean(amine_ok) * 100),
            .groups = "drop")
```

```{r clinical-plot, fig.width=9, fig.height=3.6}
participants |>
  filter(!is.na(chg_nugent)) |>
  ggplot(aes(arm, chg_nugent, fill = arm)) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 0, linetype = "dashed", colour = "grey40") +
  geom_boxplot(outlier.size = 0.5, show.legend = FALSE) +
  facet_wrap(~ start) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c(placebo = "#c46a3f", probiotic = "#2b7bb9")) +
  labs(title = "Nugent score change from pre to post, by starting group",
       subtitle = "Negative is improvement. The probiotic's edge looks bigger in the Lacto-low group, but the interaction test is not significant (p = 0.13)",
       x = NULL, y = "Nugent change (post − pre)") +
  theme_minimal()
```

**What the numbers say.** In every starting group the probiotic arm moved at
least as much as placebo, and in the Lacto-low group it moved more (Nugent
−4.2 vs −2.9; amine test 72% vs 59% converted to negative). In the
Lacto-present group the extra benefit is thin or absent (−2.5 vs −3.3; 83% vs
79%). That *pattern* is the shape you would expect if the probiotic mainly
helped people with room to improve — but none of the interaction tests come
close to significance (Nugent p = 0.13, pH p = 0.49), and the amine-test gaps
(13 vs 4 percentage points) carry no test at all here. With 45 Lacto-present
participants, differences of this size are exactly the kind that come and go
by chance. **The honest answer: no, we cannot show that the probiotic only
worked in one starting group.** The data lean that way but do not prove it.

## 5. The gene-table check

The clinical scores are coarse. The transcriptome is finer: if the probiotic
truly worked through one starting state, genes should respond to the
probiotic (a change from pre to post in the probiotic arm *beyond* placebo)
more in that state. We run DESeq2 separately in each starting group — raw
counts, sequencing batch in the design — and count genes whose
arm × visit interaction is significant (FDR < 0.1). Note the sign: with
"pre" as the reference level the interaction coefficient is flipped, so we
count p-values, which do not care about sign.

```{r deseq2, cache: true}
genes <- d$genes
responders <- function(sub) {
  g <- genes[, sub$sample_id]
  keep <- rowSums(g >= 10) >= 10
  dds <- DESeqDataSetFromMatrix(g[keep, ], colData = as.data.frame(sub),
            design = ~ rnaseq_batch + arm + time_point + arm:time_point)
  dds <- DESeq(dds, quiet = TRUE)
  res <- results(dds, name = "armprobiotic.time_pointpre")
  c(tested = sum(keep), fdr = sum(res$padj < 0.1, na.rm = TRUE),
    raw = sum(res$pvalue < 0.01, na.rm = TRUE))
}
by_start <- meta |>
  mutate(start = if_else(lacto_share >= 0.10, "present", "low"))
map_dfr(c(low = "low", present = "present"), ~
  as.data.frame(by_start |> filter(start == .x)) |> responders(),
  .id = "start") |>
  mutate(across(where(is.numeric), as.integer))
```

Almost nothing responds in either group: 0 of 14,222 tested genes in the
Lacto-low group and 2 of 14,224 in the Lacto-present group clear FDR 0.1.
Even at a permissive raw p < 0.01 the counts are small (38 and 131). For
scale, the visit itself (pre → post, both arms pooled) moved only 83 genes in
the Lacto-present group and 0 in the Lacto-low group. So at the level of gene
expression this intervention barely registered anywhere, in either starting
state — there is no subgroup hiding here that the clinical scores missed.

::: {.caution}
Two cautions on the clinical analysis. First, the Lactobacillus change itself
(pre → post share) is **not** tested here against the starting groups: those
groups are defined by baseline Lactobacillus share, so a test of that same
quantity would be circular. The Nugent, pH and amine outcomes come from the
metadata, a different table. Second, both count tables are compositional —
"a species's share went up" does not mean "there were more of it". The
clinical outcomes and the transcriptome are the tables that escape that trap,
which is another reason they are the tests that matter here.
:::

## 6. Conclusion

**The probiotic did not work only in people whose community started a certain
way — or at least, we cannot show that it did.** The point estimates lean
towards a bigger benefit in participants who started Lactobacillus-low (Nugent
−4.2 vs −2.9 against placebo), which would make biological sense: a
Lactobacillus-dominant community has less dysbiosis to fix. But the
interaction tests are not significant, the Lacto-present group has only 45
participants, and the transcriptome shows essentially no probiotic response in
either starting group. The right next step, if the question matters, is a
formal three-way test (arm × visit × starting group) in DESeq2 with more
power, or a larger cohort — not a stronger claim from these 176 people.

## Choices made

- **Starting-group definition:** Lactobacillus genus share ≥ 10% of reads at
  the pre visit. Alternative not chosen: median split (50% and 50% of
  participants but cuts through a dense part of the distribution, so tiny
  differences in reads flip people between groups).
- **Starting-group table:** microbiome species table. Alternative not chosen:
  baseline Nugent ≥ 7 (a clinical definition; would have let us test the
  microbiome, but "community state" is better measured by the community
  itself).
- **Outcomes tested:** Nugent, pH, amine test (metadata) and the gene table.
  Alternative not chosen: change in Lactobacillus share, which is circular
  against a group defined by baseline Lactobacillus.
- **Interaction test:** ordinary linear model `change ~ arm * start`.
  Alternatives not chosen: a rank-based test on amine conversion, and a
  three-way DESeq2 model `~ arm * time_point * start` fitted once on all
  samples (more powerful in principle, harder to read; a natural next step).
- **Gene filter:** ≥ 10 counts in ≥ 10 samples, per starting group.
  Alternative not chosen: the 02 report's ≥ 10 in ≥ 20 (the subgroups are
  smaller, so the looser filter keeps more genes testable).
- **Gene-model design:** `~ rnaseq_batch + arm + time_point + arm:time_point`,
  fitted separately per starting group. Alternative not chosen: including
  `discharge` and `clue_cells` as covariates (partly consequences of the
  exposure, so they would soak up signal).
- **Significance thresholds:** FDR < 0.1 for genes, p < 0.05 for the
  interaction tests; raw p < 0.01 reported alongside gene counts as a
  sensitivity check. Alternative not chosen: FDR < 0.05 (nothing changed —
  the counts only fall).
- **Samples dropped:** none. Nine participants with a missing post Nugent or
  pH value fall out of those specific means (listwise, per outcome), but no
  participant was excluded from the study.
